questions.subject: Interdisciplinary
questions.question:
Which of the following can be used as biofuel feedstock?
1. Jatropha
2. Pongamia
3. Mahua
4. Palm oil
5. Used cooking oil
questions.explanation: ALL can be used as biofuel feedstock. Jatropha and Pongamia are primary biodiesel crops in India's National Biodiesel Mission. Mahua (Madhuca indica) seeds yield oil usable as biodiesel. Palm oil is a major global biodiesel feedstock. Used Cooking Oil (UCO) is increasingly collected for biodiesel under RUCO (Repurpose Used Cooking Oil) initiative by FSSAI. This is a classic UPSC trap - testing breadth of knowledge.

questions.subject: Interdisciplinary
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Lithium reserves have been found in Jammu & Kashmir
2. India imports over 80% of its crude oil requirement
3. Rare earth minerals are essential for electric vehicle batteries
4. India has no operational lithium refining capacity currently
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 4 correct. Statement 3 is MISLEADING/WRONG - while rare earths are used in EV motors (magnets), the PRIMARY battery material is LITHIUM (with cobalt, nickel, manganese), not rare earths. Rare earths (neodymium, dysprosium) are for magnets/motors, not battery chemistry. Lithium found in Reasi (J&K, 5.9 million tonnes, 2023). India imports 85%+ crude oil. No lithium refining yet.

questions.subject: Interdisciplinary
questions.question:
With reference to 'Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism' (CBAM) of the EU:
1. It imposes a carbon levy on imports from countries without equivalent carbon pricing
2. It could affect India's steel, aluminium, and cement exports to EU
3. India has supported CBAM as a climate justice measure
4. It is designed to prevent 'carbon leakage'
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 4 correct. Statement 3 WRONG - India has OPPOSED CBAM, calling it unilateral, protectionist, and against the principle of Common But Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR). India argues developing nations shouldn't bear costs of developed nations' historical emissions. CBAM (effective Oct 2023 transitionally, full implementation 2026) affects India's iron/steel/aluminium/fertilizer exports to EU.

questions.subject: Interdisciplinary
questions.question:
Consider the following about India's semiconductor mission:
1. India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) has an outlay of ₹76,000 crore
2. Vedanta-Foxconn and ISMC are setting up fabrication plants
3. India currently manufactures chips below 7nm
4. Semiconductor fabrication requires ultra-pure water and stable power supply
questions.explanation: 1 and 4 correct. Statement 2 is OUTDATED/UNCERTAIN - Vedanta-Foxconn JV collapsed (2023). Tata Electronics and other players have since emerged but full fab status is evolving. Statement 3 WRONG - India does NOT manufacture any chips currently (no operational fab). India only does chip DESIGN (ARM, Qualcomm design centres) and ASSEMBLY/TESTING (OSAT). Sub-7nm needs EUV lithography which only ASML (Netherlands) makes.

questions.subject: Interdisciplinary
questions.question:
Which of the following correctly describes 'Green Hydrogen'?
1. Produced by electrolysis of water using renewable energy
2. The only byproduct is water
3. India targets 5 MMT annual production by 2030
4. It can replace coking coal in steel production
questions.explanation: All correct. Green hydrogen: renewable energy → electrolysis → H2 + O2 (only byproduct is water/oxygen). National Green Hydrogen Mission targets 5 MMT by 2030 (₹19,744 crore). Green hydrogen CAN replace coking coal in Direct Reduced Iron (DRI) process for steel making - this is key for decarbonizing hard-to-abate sectors. India aims to become global green hydrogen hub and exporter.

questions.subject: Interdisciplinary
questions.question:
Consider the following about the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023:
1. It applies to processing of digital personal data within India
2. It creates the Data Protection Board of India as an adjudicatory body
3. The government is exempted from the Act in the interest of national security
4. It provides for 'Right to Erasure' of personal data
questions.explanation: All correct. DPDP Act 2023 applies to digital personal data processed in India (and outside India if offering goods/services to India). Data Protection Board handles complaints/breaches. Section 17(2) exempts government for sovereignty, national security, public order. Right to Erasure (Section 12) allows individuals to request deletion of personal data. Also provides Right to Correction, Right to Grievance Redressal.

questions.subject: Interdisciplinary
questions.question:
With reference to India's Unified Payments Interface (UPI):
1. It is developed by NPCI (National Payments Corporation of India)
2. It has been linked with payment systems of Singapore, UAE, and France
3. UPI transactions are subject to Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) charges
4. UPI uses the IMPS (Immediate Payment Service) infrastructure
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 4 correct. Statement 3 WRONG - Government has mandated ZERO MDR on UPI transactions (since Jan 2020) to promote digital payments. This means merchants pay NO charges on UPI payments (unlike credit/debit cards). UPI-PayNow (Singapore), UPI-NIOPAT (UAE), UPI in France enable international interoperability. UPI rides on IMPS infrastructure for real-time settlement.

questions.subject: Interdisciplinary
questions.question:
Consider the following about 'Critical Minerals':
1. India released a Critical Minerals list that includes lithium, cobalt, and rare earths
2. India has signed critical minerals agreements with Australia and Argentina
3. KABIL (Khanij Bidesh India Ltd) is tasked with sourcing critical minerals abroad
4. India has abundant domestic reserves of all critical minerals
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG - India is critically DEPENDENT on imports for most critical minerals (lithium, cobalt, nickel, rare earths). India has some rare earth reserves but lacks processing capacity. KABIL (JV of NALCO, HCL, MECL) acquires overseas critical mineral assets. India-Australia Critical Minerals Investment Partnership signed 2022. The domestic J&K lithium find is significant but not yet operational.

questions.subject: Interdisciplinary
questions.question:
Which of the following pairs are correctly matched?
1. Sustainable Development Goal 6 - Clean Water and Sanitation
2. SDG 13 - Climate Action
3. SDG 7 - Affordable and Clean Energy
4. SDG 2 - Good Health and Well-being
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG - SDG 2 is 'Zero Hunger', NOT 'Good Health and Well-being'. SDG 3 is 'Good Health and Well-being'. UPSC frequently asks SDG numbering. Key: SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), SDG 3 (Good Health), SDG 4 (Quality Education), SDG 5 (Gender Equality), SDG 6 (Clean Water), SDG 7 (Clean Energy), SDG 13 (Climate Action), SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, Institutions).

questions.subject: Interdisciplinary
questions.question:
Consider the following about the Comptroller and Auditor General's reports:
1. CAG audited GST implementation and found leakages in input tax credit
2. CAG audit of MGNREGA found delayed wage payments and ghost workers
3. CAG reports are discussed by the Public Accounts Committee
4. The Government is legally bound to implement CAG recommendations
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 3 correct. Statement 4 WRONG - Government is NOT legally bound to implement CAG recommendations. CAG reports are advisory. PAC examines them and makes recommendations, but these too are not binding (though morally/politically significant). This is unlike judicial orders which ARE binding. CAG has flagged issues in GST (fake ITC claims), MGNREGA (delayed payments in 65% cases), defence procurement, etc.

questions.subject: Interdisciplinary
questions.question:
With reference to India's food security architecture:
1. National Food Security Act (NFSA) 2013 covers approximately 67% of the population
2. Targeted PDS divides beneficiaries into AAY and Priority Households
3. Fortification of rice and wheat is mandatory in PDS
4. One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC) enables portability of food subsidy
questions.explanation: 1, 2, 4 correct. Statement 3 WRONG - rice fortification is being implemented in phases under a government initiative (targeting PDS, mid-day meals, ICDS), but it is NOT yet fully mandatory across all PDS. NFSA: 75% rural, 50% urban (total ~67%). AAY (Antyodaya Anna Yojana): 35kg/month to poorest. Priority Households: 5kg/person/month at ₹1-3/kg. ONORC allows migrants to lift rations anywhere in India.

questions.subject: Interdisciplinary
questions.question:
Consider the following about blockchain technology applications in India:
1. RBI has launched the Digital Rupee (e₹) based on blockchain/DLT
2. Land records digitization using blockchain has been piloted in some states
3. Blockchain eliminates the need for a central authority
4. India has banned all private cryptocurrencies
questions.explanation: 1 and 2 correct. Statement 3 is OVERSIMPLIFIED/WRONG for the Digital Rupee - the e₹ (CBDC) is issued BY RBI (a central authority). While blockchain is decentralized, India's CBDC uses a permissioned/centralized DLT, NOT a fully decentralized blockchain. Statement 4 WRONG - India has NOT banned private crypto; it imposed 30% tax + 1% TDS on crypto transactions (effectively discouraging but not banning). A crypto regulation bill is still pending.
